newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Summers says strong dlr in US interests.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Summers says strong dlr in US interests.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Deputy Secretary Lawrence Summers reiterated that a strong dollar is in the interests of the United States.
"We believe that a strong currency is very much in our country's interests," said Summers, citing the positive impact on American workers' purchasing power.
Summers added that the United States does not condone use of currencies to influence global trade.

"We believe that it is wrong to ever attmept to use currencies as a tool of trade policy, because we believe the lesson of economic history is that countries cannot devalue their way to prosperity," said Summers at a luncheon.
Summers applauded Japanese efforts to stimulate domestic growth as a way to rein in Japan's burgeoning trade surplus.

"We do welcome Prime Minster (Ryutaro) Hashimoto's ongoing and oft-repeated commitment to achieving domestic demand-led growth and avoiding an excessive resurgence of Japan's external surplus," Summer said.
But the G7 leaders meeting in Denver next weekend will pay no special attention to U.S.-Japanese trade flows, though the two economies will surely be discussed, Summers said.

"It's hard to imagine a meeting of international financial officials where you will not discuss the situation of the economy of the United States and the situation of Japan. Is there something special about this moment and this meeting that will make that a particular focus? Certainly not," said Summers.
Summers added that deregulation of Japan's economy would have important benefits for Japan and the rest of the world.
"I think ongoing deregulation in Japan is very important and if pursued with vigor has great potential to improve the welfare of Japanese consumers and the Japanese economy," Summers said.

"I think it's a very important effort with very important potential benefits for Japan and, in turn, I think by spurring the Japanese economy, which is the world's second largest, carry with it important benefits for the global economy," he added.
